contract.question: Explain how large language models relate to neural networks and how they differ, including whether an LLM is a kind of neural network.

required_slots.name: direct_contrast
required_slots.description: An explicit statement of how the subjects differ

required_slots.name: dimension
required_slots.description: A named dimension along which they differ

required_slots.name: relationship
required_slots.description: How the subjects relate, such as one being a kind of the other

report.title: How Large Language Models Relate to Neural Networks

summary_claims.text: An LLM is a type of neural network that specifically uses transformer architectures.

claims.text: Transformers are described as the most common architecture for LLMs.

limitations: The evidence does not establish a general comparison of LLMs and neural networks across training objectives or scale; it gives only limited information about how LLM training differs from neural-network training more broadly.
The evidence describes text training and language tasks for LLMs, but does not establish that all LLMs use the same training data, objectives, or task set.
Only limited evidence was found for: How do LLMs differ from neural networks more generally in training data, objectives, scale, and intended tasks.

Only limited evidence was found for: What common misconceptions obscure the distinction between LLMs and neural networks—for example, whether every neural network is an LLM or whether all LLMs use the same design.
